name: unreal
label: Unreal Engine 5

maps.notes: sRGB on. Unreal's T_ prefix convention is why this preset has its own filename template.
sRGB OFF on import. R = Ambient Occlusion, G = Roughness, B = Metallic. Compression: Masks (not Default), and never let the editor 'optimise' this one.
Unreal is -Y (DirectX), and this export flips the green channel to match. BC5 compression with recomputed Z; sRGB off.
sRGB on, and the material's Emissive Intensity may exceed 1 -- keep the multiplier on the material, not in the file.

notes: Import the ORM with sRGB off and the Masks compression setting. Left at Default, the packed file is compressed as if it were colour and the roughness channel bands.
The normal map is written -Y for Unreal, so do not flip it again in the editor.
No height map in this preset: UE5 wants Nanite or WorldHeight for real displacement, and a 16-bit height PNG does nothing on its own. The height map is still in the masters folder if you want it.
Reuse a Material Instance for the values (roughness scale, normal strength) rather than duplicating the parent material per texture.
Unreal wants the three data maps packed into one ORM texture, and -Y normals. Both differ from the generic preset, which is the whole reason presets exist.
